lines.text: Clara has just moved into a tall house full of music. She heads straight for the piano, but the Butler gets there first.
Every pianist starts with the chair.

says the Butler, and he shows her, one thing at a time. Sit on the front half of the stool. Feet flat on the floor. Back tall, shoulders soft. And the stool just high enough that your arms are level with the keys, like a table top.
A true story from music history.
Nearly two hundred years ago, another girl named Clara, Clara Wieck, gave her first public concert at the Gewandhaus in Leipzig. She was nine.
She grew up to be one of the finest pianists of her day, Clara Schumann. Even she had to start at the beginning.
Feet down, back tall, arms level. The chair comes first.
